documents.title: General Robotics Fundamentals and Definitions (What is a Robot?)
documents.content: A robot is a programmable machine designed to perform physical tasks automatically or semi-autonomously. A robotic system commonly combines sensing, control or computation, and physical action through actuators. Depending on its design, a robot may operate autonomously, semi-autonomously, or under human control.

documents.title: The Science of Robotics (What is Robotics?)
documents.content: Robotics is the interdisciplinary branch of computer science and engineering focused on building, designing, and operating robots. It incorporates mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, software systems, and artificial intelligence to enable programmable machines to interact with the physical world.

documents.title: Core Robotics Systems and Subsystems (What is a Robot?)
documents.content: A robot system typically integrates several core components: a physical structure, power supply, sensors to perceive the environment, a controller or embedded computer to make decisions, and actuators to execute physical movements.

documents.title: Sensors and Perception in Robotics (What are Sensors?)
documents.content: Sensors in robotics are components used to perceive the environment or internal state. Examples include LiDAR for depth mapping, cameras for computer vision, IMUs for orientation, and encoders to track motor rotations.

documents.title: Actuators and Locomotion in Robotics (What is an Actuator?)
documents.content: An actuator is a mechanical component responsible for moving or controlling a robot mechanism. Actuators convert electrical, hydraulic, or pneumatic energy into physical force or rotational torque, driving robot joints and wheels.

documents.title: Robot Controllers and Embedded Compute (What is a Robot Controller?)
documents.content: A robot controller is the computer or embedded processing unit that executes control algorithms. It reads input data from sensors, processes trajectory plans, and outputs speed or torque command signals to the actuators.

documents.title: Classification and Types of Robots (Types of Robot?)
documents.content: Robots can be classified into different categories based on application and layout: industrial robots (robotic arms for manufacturing), mobile robots (AMRs and rovers), service robots (cleaning or hospitality), collaborative robots (Cobots working alongside humans), and autonomous robots.

documents.title: Industrial Robots and Manufacturing Automation (Explain Industrial Robots)
documents.content: Industrial robots are multi-axis programmable manipulators designed for manufacturing automation. They perform high-speed assembly, welding, material handling, painting, and packaging with sub-millimeter precision.

documents.title: Mobile Robots and Navigation Systems (Explain Mobile Robots)
documents.content: Mobile robots are vehicles capable of traversing physical environments. They use navigation algorithms (like SLAM or GPS waypoint tracking) to build maps and calculate trajectories to travel autonomously from start to goal coordinates.

documents.title: ROS 2 Quality of Service (QoS) Settings
documents.content: Quality of Service (QoS) in ROS 2 controls how nodes communicate. A QoS profile includes: 1. Reliability (Best Effort or Reliable). Reliable guarantees message delivery via retries, while Best Effort prioritizes low latency. 2. Durability (Transient Local or Volatile). Transient Local saves messages for late-joining subscribers, whereas Volatile does not. 3. History (Keep Last or Keep All). Keep Last retains a configured queue depth. 4. Depth (Queue Size). Mismatched QoS profiles, e.g., a Reliable publisher with a Best Effort subscriber, will succeed, but a Best Effort publisher with a Reliable subscriber will FAIL to connect, resulting in silent message loss.

documents.title: ROS 2 Nodes and Topics
documents.content: A node is a participant in the ROS graph that performs computations. Nodes communicate with each other through topics, services, actions, or parameters. Topics follow a publish-subscribe model where a node publishes messages to a topic, and subscribers receive them. The command 'ros2 node list' lists active nodes, while 'ros2 topic echo /topic_name' prints message streams. Nodes can have multiple publishers and subscribers for different topics.

documents.title: TF2 Transform Library
documents.content: TF2 is the transform library in ROS 2 that lets developers keep track of coordinate frames over time. A robot typically has coordinate frames like map, odom, base_link, and sensor frames (e.g. lidar_link, camera_link). TF2 builds a tree structure where every frame has exactly one parent. The default transformation tree hierarchy goes map -> odom -> base_link -> camera_link/lidar_link. Common mistakes include circular transforms, multiple parents, or coordinate frames missing a broadcaster.

documents.title: Nav2 Costmap 2D Architecture
documents.content: Nav2 uses two costmaps for path planning: the Global Costmap (used by the planner server for global pathfinding) and the Local Costmap (used by the controller server for local obstacle avoidance). Costmaps are built from layers: Static Layer (receives static map data), Obstacle Layer (reads real-time sensors like LiDAR or Depth cameras to mark/clear obstacles), Inflation Layer (inflates obstacles with a safety margin based on robot radius), and Voxel Layer (tracks 3D obstacles).

documents.title: Nav2 Core Servers
documents.content: Nav2 is composed of modular lifecycle servers: Planner Server (generates the shortest path from start to goal), Controller Server (generates velocity commands to follow the path), Smoother Server (smoothes the path for kinematic feasibility), Behavior Server (handles recovery actions like spins or back-ups when stuck), and BT Navigator (uses Behavior Trees to coordinate these servers). Nav2 requires a map -> odom transform and odom -> base_link transform to plan paths.

documents.title: NVIDIA Isaac ROS GPU Acceleration
documents.content: NVIDIA Isaac ROS is a collection of GPU-accelerated ROS 2 packages for perception and navigation. Key features include: 1. Isaac ROS Visual SLAM (gpu-accelerated stereo visual odometry and localization). 2. Isaac ROS DNN Inference (accelerated object detection, segmentation, and classification on TensorRT). 3. Image Processing (GPU-accelerated rectification, resizing, and color space conversion). These tools run on NVIDIA Jetson edge computers (like Jetson AGX Orin) or desktop GPUs to process high-resolution depth camera streams with sub-millisecond latencies.

documents.title: NVIDIA Isaac Sim Simulation platform
documents.content: NVIDIA Isaac Sim is a robotics simulation application built on Omniverse. It provides photo-realistic physics-accurate environments for training physical AI systems. Workflows include generating synthetic data (Replicator), integrating ROS 2 nodes directly via Omniverse action graphs, and performing sim-to-real domain randomization (randomizing textures, lighting, friction, and joint noise to train robust neural policies in simulation that deploy directly onto real physical hardware).

documents.title: SLAM Toolbox Mapping
documents.content: SLAM Toolbox is the default 2D SLAM library for ROS 2. It supports synchronous and asynchronous mapping, loop closure detection, map saving/loading, and localization-only mode. It publishes the map -> odom transform. Poor odometry causes map drifting. Tuning loop closure scan matching thresholds and using dynamic map updating helps maintain consistency in large-scale environments.

documents.title: AGRO-R1 Agricultural Robot Specifications
documents.name: AGRO-R1
documents.short_description: Autonomous agricultural rover designed for precision farming and intelligent crop inspection.
sensors: Dual Intel RealSense D435i depth cameras
documents.content: AGRO-R1 is an autonomous agricultural rover designed for crop inspection, precision spraying, and yield monitoring. Specifications: 1. Width: 1.2m, Length: 1.6m, Mass: 210kg. 2. Onboard Computer: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin (64GB RAM, 275 TOPS AI compute). 3. Sensors: Ouster OS1 3D LiDAR, Dual Intel RealSense D435i depth cameras, Xsens MTi-30 IMU, RTK GPS. 4. Drive System: 4WD skid-steer electric motors. 5. Payload: 60L chemical spray tank with high-frequency micro-solenoid nozzles. 6. Power: 48V Lithium-Ion Battery (8-hour runtime).

documents.title: AGRO-R1 Safety Limits and Thresholds
documents.content: AGRO-R1 has strict hardware safety limits to prevent collisions and motor damage: 1. Maximum forward velocity: 1.5 m/s. Maximum angular velocity: 1.0 rad/s. 2. Maximum incline limit: 15 degrees. 3. Maximum wheel motor current: 40A per motor. 4. Battery voltage critical low threshold: 42.0V. 5. Emergency Stop (E-Stop) activates physical brakes and cuts motor contactors if any obstacle is detected within 0.5m. 6. Maximum liquid spray pressure: 4.5 bar.

documents.title: How to Fix Coordinate Map Drift in SLAM (How do I fix coordinate map drift?)
documents.content: Coordinate map drift in SLAM occurs when cumulative sensor errors compile over time. To fix map drift, developers must enable loop closure detection in the SLAM toolbox configuration. Loop closure detects previously visited locations, computes the alignment transform, and updates the global map pose graph to correct accumulated drift between map and odom frames.

documents.title: Static Transform Publisher Launch File Setup (Show a launch file setup for a static transform publisher.)
documents.content: In ROS 2, a static transform publisher broadcasts a fixed coordinate frame transformation. A launch file setup using a static transform publisher node is configured as follows: Node(package='tf2_ros', executable='static_transform_publisher', arguments=['--x', '0.5', '--y', '0.0', '--z', '0.2', '--yaw', '0.0', '--pitch', '0.0', '--roll', '0.0', '--frame-id', 'base_link', '--child-frame-id', 'laser_link']).

documents.title: Understanding the view_frames Output in TF2 (What does 'view_frames' output represent?)
documents.content: The 'view_frames' tool in ROS 2 tf2 generates a graphical PDF diagram showing the transformation tree hierarchy. The output represents the parent-to-child connections of all active coordinate frames, the average broadcasting rate, the maximum buffer age, and the last update timestamp, allowing developers to debug frame tree continuity and locate broken link paths.

documents.title: ROS 2 Topic Command Line Interface Tools (How does 'ros2 topic info --show-details' work?)
documents.content: The command 'ros2 topic info' prints basic details about a topic. Running it with the '--show-details' flag provides extended information including the publisher/subscriber count, active node names, and the exact QoS profile configuration settings (reliability, durability, history, and depth) for each active connection.

documents.title: Nav2 Costmap Inflation Layer Parameters (Explain Nav2 global costmap inflation parameters.)
documents.content: Nav2 global and local costmap inflation settings are configured under the inflation layer using key parameters: 1. 'inflation_radius' defines the maximum distance in meters to inflate obstacles. 2. 'cost_scaling_factor' is an exponential decay factor applied to values across the inflation radius. Decreasing this factor increases the cost values farther from obstacles, causing the planner to maintain a wider safety clearance margin.

documents.title: Show code to write a custom ROS 2 publisher node.
documents.content:
To write a custom ROS 2 publisher node in Python, implement the following script:

```python
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from std_msgs.msg import String

class MinimalPublisher(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('minimal_publisher')
        self.publisher_ = self.create_publisher(String, 'topic', 10)
        self.timer = self.create_timer(0.5, self.timer_callback)
        self.i = 0

    def timer_callback(self):
        msg = String()
        msg.data = f'Hello World: {self.i}'
        self.publisher_.publish(msg)
        self.get_logger().info(f'Publishing: {msg.data}')
        self.i += 1

def main(args=None):
    rclpy.init(args=args)
    minimal_publisher = MinimalPublisher()
    rclpy.spin(minimal_publisher)
    minimal_publisher.destroy_node()
    rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

documents.title: AGRO-R1 Camera and Visual Sensor Specifications
documents.content: The AGRO-R1 agricultural rover visual sensors comprise a dual stereo configuration: 1. Two Intel RealSense D435i depth cameras positioned at the front and rear, featuring an active IR stereo sensor with a 1280x720 depth resolution, a 30 fps frame rate, and a 87° x 58° field of view. 2. One high-resolution wide-angle RGB crop inspection camera with a 12 megapixel resolution and a 120° field of view for crop classification.

documents.title: Robotics Path Planning and Quintic Trajectory Generation
documents.content: Robotics Path Planning generates smooth collision-free paths from a start pose to a goal pose. Quintic polynomial trajectory generation computes 5th-order position, velocity, and acceleration profiles s(t) = a0 + a1*t + a2*t^2 + a3*t^3 + a4*t^4 + a5*t^5 ensuring continuous C^2 motion with zero start/end acceleration.

documents.title: Forward & Inverse Kinematics and Jacobian Matrix
documents.content: Forward Kinematics (FK) computes end-effector 6D pose from joint angles using Denavit-Hartenberg (DH) matrix transformations. Inverse Kinematics (IK) calculates joint angles for a target pose using Damped Least Squares (DLS) Jacobian inversion. Yoshikawa Manipulability Index w = sqrt(det(J * J^T)) detects singular joint configurations.

documents.title: OpenCV Automated Quality Inspection 15-Stage Pipeline
documents.content: Automated Quality Inspection processes industrial parts through a 15-stage OpenCV pipeline: Read Image, Grayscale, Gaussian Blur, Thresholding, Morphology, Edge Detection, Contours, Convex Hull, Convexity Defects, Bounding Box, Dimension Measurement, Shape Analysis, Defect Detection, Confidence Scoring, and PASS/FAIL disposition.
